title: Interview pairing and calibration compact kit
summary: A compact, reusable kit for pairing interviewers, running a quick calibration, and executing a 7-day candidate-to-onboard handoff. Intended for rapid roles (interns, jr eng, contractor) and situations where we need fast, consistent decisions without heavy ceremony.
body:
Purpose:
A short, pragmatic playbook to: pair interviewers efficiently, normalize scoring across panels, and create a consistent 7-day post-offer handoff to onboarding. For lean hiring sprints where we cannot run long calibration cycles. Keep this doc as a living template (copy -> adapt).

Scope and intended audience:
- People Ops coordinators running sourcing-to-offer sprints
- Hiring managers running compact interview loops (1–3 days)
- Interviewers who will be asked to calibrate quickly before a panel
- Hiring committee members signing-off on fast offers

When to use this kit (fast-check):
- Role urgency: time-to-fill <= 14 days and role is non-exec
- Candidate pool size small (<= 30 applicants) OR high quality inbound
- Hiring manager agrees to compact loop and can commit to same-day decisions

High-level timeline (7-day fast handoff):
Day 0: Offer accepted (or verbal acceptance)
Day 1: People Ops sends candidate welcome + access request template to hiring manager
Day 2: Hiring manager provision early access (docs, repo view, buddy assigned)
Day 3: First-week orientation draft sent to candidate; scheduling for first-week check-ins
Day 4: Internal kickoff with buddy, infra access checks, payroll/admin forms reminder
Day 5: Candidate account provisioning confirmation and security checklist completed
Day 7: Formal 1:1 with manager + initial 30/60/90 draft shared

Interview pairing quick matrix (for compact loops):
- 2-interviewer panel recommended (no more than 3): 1 hiring-manager/functional + 1 cross-functional/system design or product fit (depending on role).
- Always include at least one interviewer who has performed the role recently (past 12 months).
- Prefer interviewers from the same subteam for practical ramp advice.

Pre-panel (30–60 minute prep play):
- People Ops: confirm panelers, calendar invites, candidate timezones, and links (video + test accounts).
- Hiring manager (10 mins): state the critical 2 success outcomes for first 90d (write them as bullet lines).
- Interviewers (15–30 mins): read candidate resume + role spec, review shared rubric, agree on focus areas.
- Quick calibration: 10-min sync where panelers run through 3 anchor examples (see Rubric anchors below) and align on what a 1/3/5 looks like.

Calibration rubric (compact):
Scale: 1 (miss) / 3 (meets baseline) / 5 (exceeds)
Dimensions (pick 3–4 for each role):
- Problem decomposition (logic + clarity)
- Code: correctness + readable approach (use of tests, edge cases)
- System thinking (when applicable): tradeoffs, scaling constraints
- Communication and collaboration (how they iterate with you)
- Culture-fit signals: curiosity, ownership, feedback loop

Rubric anchors (3 quick examples all interviewers should agree on):
- Anchor A (score=5): Candidate names a clear approach, writes a working prototype within time, notes relevant edge-cases and test ideas, articulates tradeoffs, asks clarifying Qs.
- Anchor B (score=3): Candidate gets to a correct direction with help, some gaps remain (untested edge cases), communicates moderately.
- Anchor C (score=1): Candidate punts, no clear approach, misses obvious constraints, or shows poor collaboration signals.

Scoring & decision protocol (compact):
- Each interviewer submits a single numeric score (1/3/5) + 2-line justification within 2 hours of interview.
- Hiring manager aggregates: if all >=3 and at least one 5 -> recommend hire.
- If mixed (one 1 and one 5): convene 30-min adjudication with a neutral calibrator (People Ops or senior IC) within 24 hours.
- No autopromote: hiring manager must write a 1-paragraph business case for exceptional hires (rare).

Panel notes template (quick copy):
- Candidate: [name] | Role: [title] | Date: [yyyy-mm-dd]
- Interviewers: [A], [B]
- Top 2 strengths:
- Top 2 concerns:
- Score (1/3/5) and 1-sentence rationale

Candidate handoff checklist (from offer to day 7):
- People Ops: send official offer packet + welcome guide (same day as verbal acceptance).
- Hiring manager: share 30/60/90 draft within 48h of acceptance.
- Buddy: assigned and intro email sent within 24h.
- Engineering ops: requests for repo access and cloud dev sandbox submitted within 24h.
- Security: new-hire IAM request created and flagged for expedite.
- IT equipment ticket opened (if hybrid/on-prem).
- Payroll: new-hire paperwork reminder and link.
- Candidate: first-week logistics (times, points-of-contact, benefits FAQ).
- People Ops: schedule Day 7 manager 1:1 and Day 14 onboarding pulse.

Email templates (boilerplate — copy/adapt):
- Offer acceptance -> candidate: concise welcome + next steps + who to contact.
- Intro to buddy -> short context + 3 suggested sync topics.
- Panel feedback request -> quick one-liner template for post-interview submissions.

Operational notes / common failure modes:
- Late rubric submission: escalate to hiring manager; if >48h, paneling considered stale and candidate moved to cold queue.
- Misaligned expectations: if hiring manager expectations differ from rubric, pause and re-calibrate before next panel.
- Access bottleneck: have a pre-approved expedite IAM token pool for compact hires (ask infra/security to maintain).

Metrics for this kit (track after each sprint):
- Time from first interview -> offer (target <= 7 days).
- Offer acceptance to first-day-ready (target <= 7 days).
- % panels with rubric submitted within 2h (target >= 90%).
- Post-30-day retention signal (tracked in People Ops).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we create a small training workshop (30m) for new interviewers on the 1/3/5 compact rubric? (Marcus to pilot Q2 2025)
- Can infra/security confirm the expedite IAM pool SLA? (SLO needed)
- Decide whether contractor offers follow same 7-day handoff or a 3-day condensed variant.

Notes to self (informal):
- This is intentionally sparse — keep friction low for small roles.
- Avoid engineering-heavy panels for jr roles; focus on learning potential and curiosity.
- Keep a copy history: people-ops/hiring-kits/compact -> make it searchable in Confluence.

Appendix: quick checklist card (single paragraph to send to interviewers):
"Prep: read resume + role spec, run through 3 anchors (A/B/C), pick top 2 signals you care about. After interview: submit 1-line score (1/3/5) + 1-sentence rationale within 2h. Hiring manager will aggregate and call within 24h if needed."

Version notes: v0.1 draft created 2025-02-18 by Aisha. In review 2025-03-02.
